title: Console compact telemetry cuts: strategy, staged acceptance criteria, fallback policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Narrow the Console observability surface for GA by reducing telemetry tiles, deferring full-trace ingest, and shipping robust fallbacks so we meet latency and cost targets while providing actionable insights for customers.

Background: The original PRD included 10+ insight tiles, full per-request trace ingestion, and per-token cost breakdowns by route. Early infra estimates and trace retention costs put the hosted economics at 30% over target for self-serve customers. UX research shows 3 tiles cover 80% of initial user needs; the rest provide diminishing returns for MVP. This ticket captures the scoped-down approach, acceptance criteria for each staged cut, and the fallback policy if backend sampling or rollout limits are hit.

Scope decisions (what we will ship in the compact MVP):
- Essential dashboard cardset (3 cards): Route throughput, 95th latency, and per-route cost delta (high-level).
- Aggregated cost breakdown: only per-route totals and token buckets for top-5 routes. No token-level breakdown per API key.
- Trace surface: sample-first traces (1% global sampling) + quick-link to on-demand deeper traces for Dedicated customers only. No full-streaming trace ingestion for Hosted tier.
- Inspectors: one lightweight request inspector that surfaces model, sequence length, and cache hit/miss counts; advanced request inspectors deferred.
- Rollout controls: gated canary for 10% of users with automatic rollback on cost or latency regressions.

Out of scope (deferred to post-MVP):
- Per-token detailed charge visualization per-request.
- Full 100% trace capture and retention for hosted customers.
- Multi-card customboards and ad-hoc card creation.
- Deep APM-style spans and distributed trace linking to infra metrics.

Why this cut: Reduces backend storage and ingest costs, minimizes initial UI complexity, and preserves developer-facing value (visibility into cost/latency trends). Keeps path to restore features when economics/infra optimize.

Rollout/fallback policy (critical):
- If backend sampling queue exceeds 70% capacity for 3 consecutive minutes, automatically reduce sampling to 0.25% and flag for on-call.
- If cost-per-customer projection exceeds budget threshold (TBD metric) during canary, pause rollout and revert to static aggregated cards with 24-hour refresh.
- Dedicated customers retain opt-in for full trace capture via a separate config and billing line item.

Metrics for success (used by acceptance criteria):
- Mean dashboard load time < 350ms for users in region.
- Telemetry ingest cost delta <= +8% over baseline infra budget for first 30 days post-launch.
- 95% of users can find the top-3 signals within 15s of onboarding (measured by UX task completion in beta).
- No production incidents attributed to tracing pipeline for 30 days after rollout.

Linked artifacts and references:
- PRD (trimmed): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CONSOLE/Observability+PRD+compact
- UX task notes (beta): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/observability-beta-ux
- Infra cost model: https://docs.redwood.ai/infracosts/console-telemetry-2025-02
- Engineering playbook for sampling and fallback: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/tree/main/trace-sampling

Notes on trade-offs and alternatives considered:
- Full trace ingest with aggressive retention TTLs: rejected because it still exceeded cost envelope and increased complexity for earliest customers.
- Keep all cards but lazy-load details: rejected due to backend projection showing high peak load on UI queries.
- Offer per-customer opt-in during signup: deferred to post-MVP for clarity of onboarding and implementation complexity.

Next steps and immediate action items:
- PM to finalize the exact cost budget threshold and share with Eng by 2025-02-21.
- ENG to implement sampling/fallback hooks and expose sampling rate metric (ENG-78421).
- Design to produce compact-card mocks and responsive behavior for mobile (due 2025-02-28).
- Security to review data retention settings for tracing deferred captures (security review not required for compact MVP, but settings must be auditable).

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha Patel), Design (Maya Singh), Eng (Liam Chen), Observability SRE (Rory McKenna), Sales/CS (Priya Rao).
acceptance_criteria: Three dashboard cards deployed and visible in the Console for beta users
Dashboard mean load time < 350ms in staging and production canary
Sampling controls implemented: adjustable global sampling percent and automatic throttle on overload
Cost delta for telemetry ingest validated end-to-end and within +8% of target in a 7-day smoke test
Rollout gating works: canary defaults to 10% and can be paused/rolled back by the on-call flow
Dedicated customers can enable on-demand full-trace capture via separate config and billing opt-in
